resolution_rationale: No existing issue identities were supplied. This review preserves unresolved dependencies and makes no correctness or execution claim.

scope_limitations: Unsuccessful Apply futures do not establish that a command cannot take effect.
Explicit user snapshot restoration is outside the preservation guarantee.
items.explanation: The Apply document promises durable quorum storage before application, and the FSM interface requires majority commitment before Apply. These attributed expectations establish the goal for ordinary command processing independently of the accumulator's implementation. API comments explicitly permit uncertain outcomes after leadership loss and loss of effects after user restore; the goal's exclusions preserve those qualifications. Applicability is provisionally supported.
items.alternatives: Single-entry FSM delivery and BatchingFSM delivery both retain the commitment prerequisite. Neither requires all followers to finish application before the leader applies a command.
items.counterexample_reasoning: The goal could fail despite correct accumulator arithmetic if reports misrepresent stored prefixes or the delivery path applies a command beyond the supported index. Those possibilities concern discharge of the goal, not whether the documented guarantee applies.
limitations: The applicable durable-storage semantics and governing membership history remain unresolved.
The commitment-to-command delivery correlation is not established by the supplied implementation ranges.
The grounding's BatchApplyCh qualification is not independently supported by the attached materials and is not relied upon here.

scope_limitations: This judgment concerns the accumulator's responsibility, not end-to-end Apply correctness.
items.explanation: The commitment comments explicitly describe monotonically increasing quorum support and require replication of the first index of the leader term before marking anything committed. Together with the documented majority-commitment prerequisite, these statements support the obligation independently of the particular sorting implementation. Evaluating support at each advancement preserves the distinction between a new commitment decision and retaining an earlier decision after membership changes.
items.alternatives: A different accumulator algorithm could satisfy the same responsibility without sorting. Requiring every retained commit index to have fresh support in every later voter set would impose a stronger property than this obligation.
items.counterexample_reasoning: An advancement supported by fewer than a strict majority of tracked voter reports, a decrease, or an advancement below the supplied term threshold would contradict the stated local responsibility. No such execution has been demonstrated.
limitations: Correct startIndex initialization, membership admission and report provenance remain unverified conditions for interpreting the accumulator as real consensus commitment.

scope_limitations: Durability, FSM delivery and client completion are outside the checked obligation.
The obligation specifies advancement safety, not eventual advancement or notification delivery.
items.explanation: Constructor initialization, report consumption, voter-set replacement and recalculation cover the local state transitions relevant to the obligation. For n tracked voters, the ascending element at floor((n-1)/2) has at least floor(n/2)+1 reports at or above it. This explains correspondence of the arithmetic to strict-majority report support, without proving an executed model or the reports' truth. Configuration validation checks identifiers and voter presence, but does not establish legal transition timing.
items.alternatives: Maintaining the previous commit index after a configuration change is compatible with an advancement-only obligation. Local writes, ordinary replication, pipelines and snapshots can supply evidence through different producer paths.
items.counterexample_reasoning: All clauses can hold while a falsely attributed report or an inadmissible membership history yields unsupported real application. The existing assumptions and boundary relation retain this insufficiency rather than treating the obligation as sufficient for G_apply.
limitations: Local-write and alternative remote producers are not fully represented.
Caller ordering and report lifetime across membership or address changes remain unresolved.

scope_limitations: The binding covers construction, not caller correctness.
items.explanation: The declaration at line 35 and behavior range 35–48 identify newCommitment. The body selects Voter identities, initializes their reports and commitIndex to zero, and records the supplied startIndex. Its association with O_commit and direct initialization use in U_commit are supported.
items.alternatives: Configuration validation and leadership-term initialization belong to callers; this constructor does not perform them.
items.counterexample_reasoning: An incorrect supplied threshold could undermine actual commitment even when this constructor copies it faithfully. The binding does not claim to verify that producer responsibility.
limitations: Caller initialization and admissible configuration prerequisites remain unread.

scope_limitations: The binding does not establish protocol legality of membership transitions.
items.explanation: The declaration at line 53 and range 53–64 identify setConfiguration. Under the mutex, it replaces the tracked voter map, preserves reports for retained IDs, initializes newly tracked IDs through zero-valued lookup, and recalculates. These operations directly implement the voter-set transition relevant to O_commit and the selected history coverage.
items.alternatives: The current method retains earlier commitment decisions instead of resetting commitIndex. This is consistent with evaluating quorum support only on new advancements.
items.counterexample_reasoning: Changing the voter set can cause advancement without a new match call. A later checker must therefore include this path. Reusing an ID for a different storage history would raise a producer or membership question beyond the map operation.
limitations: Permitted call ordering and continuity of server identity across address changes remain unresolved.

scope_limitations: The binding consumes reports and does not verify their storage evidence.
items.explanation: The declaration at line 77 and range 77–84 identify match. The body accepts only increasing reports for currently tracked voter IDs and invokes recalculation under the mutex. Its association with O_commit and direct consumer role are supported by both the method's input contract and its body.
items.alternatives: Untracked and non-increasing reports leave the accumulator unchanged. Evidence validation may occur upstream and is not implemented here.
items.counterexample_reasoning: An inflated report for a tracked ID could be accepted while all local update rules hold. This demonstrates why local report-support checks cannot establish durable-prefix support.
limitations: Leadership-instance, peer and stored-prefix provenance of reports remain unverified.

scope_limitations: Notification consumption and FSM delivery are outside this behavior range.
items.explanation: The declaration at line 88 and range 88–104 identify recalculate. It handles an empty voter map, computes the order statistic, applies the advancement and startIndex guards, and invokes notification after assigning commitIndex. O_commit is the direct responsibility; the G_apply association correctly describes an upstream contribution rather than application itself.
items.alternatives: Other quorum algorithms could implement the same contract. Notification scheduling is a separate handoff from computing the supported index.
items.counterexample_reasoning: Correct recalculation would not prevent a consumer from applying an unrelated or later command. Neither this binding nor its goal association establishes that missing correspondence.
limitations: The implementation and consumption of notification are not established by this binding.

scope_limitations: U_commit uses this binding as input context and does not check O_append_evidence.
items.explanation: The declaration at line 202 and behavior range 202–295 identify replicateTo. The supplied body calls request construction and transport, stops on a response term greater than the request term, and calls updateLastAppended after success. The association explicitly describes an unresolved helper handoff. U_commit selects this context through R_commit_append and does not count the producer obligation as checked.
items.alternatives: The snapshot branch is visible but its progress semantics are unread; pipeline progress is also outside the resolved path. The response-term comparison is not itself a complete request or peer identity check.
items.counterexample_reasoning: Success alone does not reveal which index the helper reports, particularly for an empty request. A plausible helper error could leave the accumulator arithmetic correct while invalidating actual support.
limitations: setupAppendEntries and updateLastAppended remain unresolved callees.
Transport correlation, storage durability and alternative progress paths remain unverified.

scope_limitations: The relation concerns normal leader processing and represents only one necessary contribution to G_apply.
items.explanation: The goal-to-obligation direction and necessary-component interpretation of depends_all are supported by the documented Apply sequence. However, the actual leader notification consumer and processLogs implementation are absent. The available FSM code consumes commit tuples without establishing how their command identities and indexes were selected. The implementing handoff required by this review therefore remains unresolved; the relation should remain unconfirmed.
items.alternatives: Single-entry and batch delivery can share an upstream commitment prerequisite. Follower processing instead receives a leader commit index, so the local leader accumulator is not a direct consumer path for every FSM invocation.
items.counterexample_reasoning: O_commit could hold while delivery selects an entry beyond the committed prefix or from the wrong context. The current graph acknowledges that the corresponding delivery obligation is missing; this review cannot treat the one represented dependency as sufficient.
limitations: Actual leader consumption, command-index correlation and delivery filtering require additional source.
The missing delivery obligation remains substantive incomplete decomposition of G_apply.

scope_limitations: The relation records the ordinary remote replication boundary, not every match-report producer.
items.explanation: The direction from the accumulator consumer to the remote evidence responsibility is appropriate. match states a stored-prefix input contract; replicateTo acts on success; appendEntries performs predecessor checks and storage operations before success. Because the reporting helper and storage guarantees are unresolved, boundary accurately records an unestablished producer guarantee. It does not assert proved support or require O_append_evidence to be checked in U_commit.
items.alternatives: Leader-local persistence, pipelined replication and snapshot installation require their own producer accounting. They are not interchangeable with the selected non-pipelined handoff.
items.counterexample_reasoning: Incorrect index reporting, lost storage evidence or stale peer attribution could violate the producer responsibility while leaving O_commit's report arithmetic satisfied. This is precisely the unresolved boundary represented by the relation.
limitations: The helper's exact index and identity mapping remain unread.
The LogStore contract and behavior after deletion followed by failed append are unresolved.
No durability or request-correlation guarantee is inferred from the transport interface alone.

scope_limitations: Only O_commit is selected for checking.
The unit does not establish distributed execution legality, end-to-end Apply correctness or goal observability.
items.explanation: The question, four direct accumulator bindings and O_commit form a coherent bounded local scope. B_replicate_to is explicitly contextual through the selected boundary relation. Mutex-protected accumulator mutations support examining local transitions without inventing a network-wide schedule. The history coverage correctly calls for interleaved reports and voter-set changes within the same commitment instance, and goal_observable=false avoids claiming an application witness.
items.alternatives: This unit can investigate accumulator behavior while producer and delivery responsibilities remain separate work. Adding those responsibilities to the checked set would require sourced expansion rather than treating input context as coverage.
items.counterexample_reasoning: Independent reachability of initialization, match and configuration replacement would not establish the requested same-instance sequence. Also, a passing local check could coexist with a wrong startIndex, inadmissible membership history or unsupported application.
limitations: No model, checker, executable harness or actual observations were supplied; executability, nonvacuity and calibration have not been demonstrated.
The eventual model must retain configuration-triggered advancement and distinguish advancement-time support from later voter-set changes.
Caller legality, producer truth and the unresolved R_apply_commit handoff remain open.

requests.reason: Locate and inspect leader commitment-notification handling and its command-delivery handoff for R_apply_commit. Establish the consumed index and relevant leadership/configuration context; these locations are requested for inspection, not asserted as verified anchors.

Locate and inspect log dispatch and processLogs near the supplied appendEntries declaration. Determine how committed indexes select log entries and commit tuples for FSM delivery, including identity and range filtering, to assess the missing R_apply_commit handoff.
